- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.10) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–4% above recent high.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.20) for 3+ consecutive days, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to counteract mean reversion bias.
- Model consistently underestimates in the 10–15 day horizon; increase forecast by 0.8–1.2% for that window.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; add 0.3–0.7% to forecast at that point.
- Forecasting 30-day ahead often misses late-stage momentum; add 0.5–1.0% to final 5–7 days if sentiment turns bullish.
